summary: Completed backend regression and live API/UI checks. Core health, login, auth/me, dashboard, ticket/comment flow, tenant isolation, disabled integration contracts, requester portal creation, and mobile menu passed.

critical.issue: Requester role can directly list every ticket in its organization and retrieve arbitrary same-organization ticket details; requester-safe portal should restrict direct ticket reads to requester-owned tickets (or deny these routes). Requester can also post comments to arbitrary same-organization tickets through the generic comment endpoint.

minor.issue: Live public URL returns the React SPA HTML rather than the FastAPI OpenAPI schema; /api/openapi.json returns 404. OpenAPI is therefore not available through the ingress URL.

ui_bugs.issue: React runtime overlay reports `TypeError: destroy is not a function` after navigation. Effects pass promise-returning load functions directly to useEffect (`useEffect(load, ...)`), causing React to treat the Promise as cleanup.

action_items: Restrict requester direct ticket/detail/comment access to requester-owned tickets or enforce requester-specific endpoints.
Expose FastAPI OpenAPI under the public ingress path (for example /api/openapi.json or ingress mapping).
Wrap promise-returning load functions in useEffect callbacks that do not return the Promise, fixing the React destroy cleanup crash.
critical_code_review_comments: Authorization is inconsistent: requester portal has /api/my/tickets scoping, but generic ticket and comment routes only scope organization_id and permit requester access to other employees' tickets.
FastAPI defaults are not ingress-compatible because docs/openapi routes lack the /api prefix.
seed_data_creation: Existing regression test created isolated temporary organizations and test comments; live UI created one TEST employee portal request.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Four existing pytest tests passed. Teams card returned five actions and not_configured; Teams action safely returned ok=false; AI analyze and voice status were disabled as configured. Recheck requester authorization, OpenAPI routing, and React navigation cleanup after fixes.
rca of the issue: Requester authorization gap is caused by generic ticket/detail/comment handlers filtering only organization_id while /api/my/tickets filters requester_email. React crash is caused by useEffect(load, ...) where load returns the axios Promise, which React interprets as an effect destructor. OpenAPI routing mismatch occurs because FastAPI defaults /openapi.json and /docs are not prefixed with /api while the ingress sends only /api routes to backend.
